pw_slow_hash.evidence: server.py:102-104 salt = salt or secrets.token_bytes(16); hashlib.scrypt(password.encode("utf-8"), salt=salt, n=SCRYPT_N, r=SCRYPT_R, p=SCRYPT_P
pw_slow_hash.note: scrypt with a random 16-byte salt per password, N=2**14, r=8, p=1 (server.py:98)

token_csprng.note: Tokens are random, not signed. The server stores only a SHA-256 hash of each token (server.py:122-123, 500).

no_hardcoded_secret.note: There is no signing key at all. The only secret-like value is the dummy hash, and it is built from random bytes at startup.

token_expiry.evidence: server.py:302 if row is None or row["expires_at"] < time.time(): raise ApiError(401, ...)
token_expiry.note: Login sets expires_at = now + SESSION_DAYS * 86400, which is 30 days (server.py:501).

logout_revokes.evidence: server.py:374 conn.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE token_hash = ?", (token_hash(token),))
logout_revokes.note: POST /api/logout deletes the session row on the server

owner_checks.evidence: server.py:308 "SELECT * FROM notes WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?"
owner_checks.note: own_note() runs before read, update and delete (server.py:407) and before share and unshare (server.py:433). The UPDATE and DELETE statements also filter on user_id (419, 427, 439, 447).

login_rate_limit.evidence: server.py:488-489 if login_blocked(keys): raise ApiError(429, "too many failed logins...")
login_rate_limit.note: Limits are 10 failures per email and 100 per IP in a 15-minute window (server.py:130-132). The counts are kept in memory only, so a restart resets them.

sql_parameterized.note: Every statement that takes user input uses ? placeholders (e.g. 299, 308, 397, 419, 472, 491). None are built with f-strings or string concatenation.

xss_safe_render.evidence: static/app.js:101 btn.textContent = note.title; static/app.js:217-218 $("shared-title").textContent = note.title; $("shared-body").textContent = note.body;
xss_safe_render.note: The editor fills its inputs through .value (app.js:119-120). There is no innerHTML or insertAdjacentHTML in the static files.

security_headers.note: _common_headers() is called by send_json, send_empty and send_static, so every response gets these headers
